name: 598 Brannan Street
acresNote: Planning Commission packet for the June 6, 2019 approval (case 2012.0640): four lots on Assessor's Block 3777 (045, 050, 051 and 052) "collectively encompassing approximately 4.5 acres", with a total area of 195,467 sq ft. Lot 052 has since been split into lots 176 and 177; the parcels drawn come to about 4.5 acres.

program.notes: As approved on June 6, 2019: three office buildings with about 922,737 gross sq ft of office, about 60,471 sq ft of ground-floor retail and PDR space and a 5,546 sq ft child care center, built in two phases. Building 1, at 5th and Brannan streets, is 11 stories and 160 ft (180 ft with the rooftop mechanical screen), with 289,087 sq ft of office; Building 2, at 5th and Welsh streets, is 13 stories and 185 ft (205 ft), using a 25-ft height bonus for providing the affordable housing site and the park, with 422,049 sq ft of office; Building 3, on Bryant Street, is 10 stories and 150 ft (170 ft), with 211,601 sq ft of office and the child care center. Also a public park of about 39,661 sq ft (0.91 acres) at the center of the site, given to the City and built by the developer, about 19,336 sq ft of privately owned public open space and 200 underground parking spaces. In place of building affordable homes, the developer gave the City a 12,800 sq ft site at 160 Freelon Street; the 2019 approval expected a building of up to 72 affordable homes there. The building now under construction on it has 85 homes: 84 affordable to extremely low- and low-income households (25% set aside as supportive housing) and a manager's unit, in 15 studios, 24 one-bedrooms, 22 two-bedrooms and 23 three-bedrooms. Planning's project record counts all 85 as affordable.

developer: Brannan & Bryant Street, LLC, an affiliate of Tishman Speyer (the office buildings; named in the 2019 approval and the Mayor's Office of Housing's land dedication letter); 160 Freelon Housing Partners, L.P. (the affordable housing building)
publicPartners: Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development (affordable housing site)
San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (exchange of 639 Bryant Street for 2000 Marin Street)
San Francisco Board of Supervisors (land exchange, Board File 180550)
San Francisco Department of Building Inspection
stageNote: Only the affordable housing is being built. The nine-story building with 85 affordable homes at 160 Freelon Street, on the land the project gave the City, has been under construction since July 15, 2025 (DBI permit 202209283327); DBI passed a partial rough-frame inspection on Sept 24, 2026. The three office buildings haven't started: DBI issued the site permits for Buildings 1 and 2 on March 17, 2021 and the existing buildings at 590-598 Brannan and 645 Bryant streets were demolished that year, but no construction on them is recorded, a 2021 shoring permit was cancelled in 2024, Building 3's site permit has been pending since 2019, and Planning's project record reads "On Hold". Planning records from 2025 and 2026 concern a parking lot on the site.

timeline.event: SF Planning opens case 2012.0640 for the redevelopment of 598 Brannan Street.
Brannan & Bryant Street, LLC applies for a Large Project Authorization for three office buildings.
Planning Commission certifies the Central SoMa Plan EIR (Motion 20182); the plan names the site Key Development Site 5, the "Park Block".
The Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development conditionally accepts 160 Freelon Street as the project's affordable housing land dedication.
Planning Department finds the project covered by the Central SoMa Plan EIR (community plan evaluation).

Planning Commission approves the project: Large Project Authorization (Motion 20459), 711,136 sq ft of office allocation for Phase 1 (Motion 20460) and a fee waiver agreement for the public park (Resolution 20461).
Site permit applications for Buildings 1 and 2 are filed with DBI; Building 3's follows on Dec 13, 2019.
Planning Commission approves 211,601 sq ft of office allocation for Phase 2, Building 3 (Motion 20816).
DBI issues the site permits for Buildings 1 (11 stories) and 2 (13 stories).
Demolition of the buildings at 590-598 Brannan Street and 645 Bryant Street passes final inspection.
Planning approves the 85-home affordable housing building at 160 Freelon Street (record 2022-008873PRJ, filed for the state's streamlined approval of supportive housing, AB 2162).
DBI issues the building permit for 160 Freelon Street (permit 202209283327).
Construction of the affordable housing building at 160 Freelon Street begins (DBI first construction document).

nextMilestone: Completion of the affordable housing at 160 Freelon Street; for the office buildings, a start of construction, for which no date is on record.
summary: Three office buildings of 150 to 185 ft, with about 923,000 sq ft of office space, around a new one-acre public park at 5th and Brannan streets, Central SoMa's "Park Block" key site. Approved in 2019; the old buildings were demolished in 2021, but the office buildings haven't started. On land the project gave the City, a nine-story building with 85 affordable homes at 160 Freelon Street is under construction.
massingNotes: Added at Matthew's request (2026-10-19). Boundary: DataSF parcels (acdm-wktn), block 3777 lots 045, 050 and 051 and lots 176 and 177, which replaced the approval's lot 052 in 2025; 4.5 acres as drawn; official. Massing (pipeline/bam_pipeline/sites/massing_598_brannan.py): the three office buildings' roof outlines and ground-floor outlines traced from the 2019 plan set's roof plan and site plan (packet pp. 116 and 115, vector drawings), each registered to six or seven lot corners (RMS 0.2 m), drawn as the roof outline at the approved roof height (160, 185 and 150 ft) and the rest of the ground floor up to where each building steps back (31, 73 and 76 ft). Upper floors that overhang are drawn to the ground; terraces, mechanical screens and the park are not drawn. Illustrative, drawn as entitled. The affordable housing lot at 160 Freelon Street (lot 176) is outlined as under construction; its building's height in feet isn't in the records read.
